papers_read.title_as_printed: Predicting Mild Cognitive Impairment in Type 2 Diabetes: A Machine Learning Approach (Li et al., Journal of Diabetes Research 2025, Article ID 7304414)
Prediction and validation of mild cognitive impairment in occupational dust exposure population based on machine learning (Cai et al., Ecotoxicology and Environmental Safety 2024;285:117111)

what_each_reports.P-343: SVC on seven routine variables (age, education, eGFR, SBP, BMI, T2DM duration, a genetic-programming glucolipid 'GCA' index) for clinically diagnosed MCI (AAN 2018 criteria, Beijing MoCA < 26) in 2074 T2DM inpatients (Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital): internal cross-validated AUC 0.74 +/- 0.04 (tuned SVC; tuned AdaBoost 0.76); external validation in the DECODE cohort AUC 0.80. The extract drops decimal points ('0 74 ± 0 04'); decoded as 0.74 +/- 0.04 from the paper's own tables.
what_each_reports.P-19: XGBoost on baseline characteristics (education, age, work years, SSRS, HAMA and others) for MoCA-screened MCI (MoCA <= 26) in 1938 dust-exposed coal miners: training AUC 0.959, internal validation AUC 0.795 (logistic 0.816), and AUC 0.913 on an additional test set of 351 miners (50 MCI).

quantity_a: ROC-AUC of a routine-clinical-variable SVC for clinically diagnosed MCI vs normal cognition in hospitalised Chinese T2DM patients aged >= 40, the quoted 0.80 being the external DECODE-cohort figure (internal 0.74).
quantity_b: ROC-AUC of an XGBoost model on occupational, psychological and demographic variables for MoCA-screened MCI vs normal in working-age dust-exposed coal miners (mean age about 43-49), the quoted 0.913 being a 351-person additional test set (internal validation 0.795).
incompatible_if_same: No. Even on their own terms the figures overlap once like splits are compared: P-19's internal validation AUC (0.795) is essentially P-343's external AUC (0.80); the 0.113 gap exists only because the record sets P-343's external figure against P-19's separate test-set figure. Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: match in the broad sense (cross-sectional MCI vs non-MCI detection); the registry codes P-19 as T2 and the record says T1 for both.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Nanjing Drum Tower T2DM inpatients (+ DECODE, NHANES III for validation) vs a single Huainan coal-mine occupational health cohort. The record itself says dataset_equal 'No'; no waiver on record.
gates.validation_tier: match at the tier level: both report a held-out cohort beyond internal splitting (DECODE for P-343; a separately recruited 351-miner test set for P-19).
gates.modality_family: match in family (clinical/tabular) but the predictor sets are disjoint apart from age and education (renal, blood-pressure, glucolipid and diabetes-duration variables vs work years, social support and anxiety scales).

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: same metric type (ROC-AUC) but different populations behind the MCI label (older T2DM inpatients vs middle-aged coal miners), different MCI definitions (AAN 2018 clinical criteria with MoCA < 26 vs a MoCA <= 26 screen alone), and different predictor sets.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: the compared figures are 0.80 and 0.913; P-19's training AUC 0.959 is not the compared figure and is below 0.97.
independence: Independent of each other. Note P-19 and P-20 are the same paper (identical PDF text; summaries.md Paper 19 and Paper 20 are '1-s2.0-S0147651324011874-main (1).pdf' and '-main.pdf'), so C-185 duplicates this record.
grounds: The populations behind the shared MCI label differ: hospitalised T2DM patients aged 40 or over in P-343 against working-age dust-exposed coal miners in P-19.
The MCI definitions differ: clinical AAN 2018 criteria in P-343 against a MoCA <= 26 screen in P-19.
The predictor sets differ apart from age and education, so the AUCs belong to different models, not to one estimand.
The dataset-family gate fails, as the record itself states, and no waiver is recorded.
The recorded gap comes from pairing unlike splits: P-19's internal validation AUC (0.795) matches P-343's external AUC (0.80).

evidence_quotes.quote: with an AUC of 0 74 ± 0 04, an F1 score of 0 62 ± 0 06, and a recall of 0 74 ± 0 09 in internal validation. External validation with the DECODE cohort yielded an AUC of 0.80, an F1 score of 0.80, and a recall of 0.89.

This cross-sectional study prospectively enrolled adult inpatients diagnosed with T2DM from the Department of Endocrinology at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital over the period from January 2016 to December 2023.
Ultimately, variables including age, education, eGFR, SBP, BMI, T2DM duration, and the previously derived representation index were incorporated into model development.
A total of 1938 miners were included in the study.

XGBoost (training set: AUC=0.959, validation set: AUC=0.795) and Logistic Regression (training set: AUC=0.818, validation set: AUC=0.816) models exhibited superior predictive performance. Results from the test set showed that the AUC of the XGBoost model (AUC=0.913) outperformed the Logistic Regression model (AUC=0.778).
A total score of ≤26 is considered to indicate that there may be mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and a total score of > 26 is defined as a normal population.

record_defects: resolution reads 'Rejected: Task, dataset, or modality mismatch' while resolution_note reads 'Confirmed genuine: Same metric type (AUC)'; the two fields contradict each other.
resolution_status is partially_resolved_candidate, but no named third study showing a separating condition is recorded; the bridging list is a set of unrelated performance figures.
claim_a's 'AUC 0.80' is P-343's external DECODE figure; its internal cross-validated AUC is 0.74 +/- 0.04, which the record omits.
claim_b's 'AUC 0.913' is P-19's additional 351-miner test set; its internal validation AUC is 0.795, which the record omits.

Registry P-343: Sample_N_Approx '074' (the paper has 2074), Dataset 'NHANES' (development cohort is Nanjing Drum Tower inpatients; NHANES III is a secondary validation with no AUC), Validation_Type 'not reported' (external validation performed).
P-19 and P-20 are one paper; the pair of records C-184 and C-185 double-counts one comparison.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Evidence that the two models were evaluated on a common population with a common MCI definition; nothing in either paper does this.
